title: Cluster 1 — the Meltwash basin
about: Machine-readable geography of cluster 1. This is the data the world map is DRAWN FROM; the SVG is a view of it, never the source of truth. Every proper noun here already exists in the Cartographer's document (A1) or content/story/canon.md — nothing is invented.

coordinateSystem.convention: x increases EAST, y increases SOUTH (north is smaller y) — inherited unchanged from content/maps/atlas-frontier.md
coordinateSystem.origin: x=0 is the west edge of the sheet (open sea); y=0 is the hard parchment edge at the top (the ice). A1 §2: the land is roughly 190 km north-south and 150 km east-west.
coordinateSystem.tolerance: Positions are authored to reproduce A1 §5.1's straight-line distances within ~8%. A1 §5.3 is explicit that the world preserves topology, adjacency, ordering and terrain — NOT exact metric distance — so these coordinates are a faithful schematic, not a survey. `distances[].deltaPct` records the residual for every canon-bearing leg.

coastline.note: A1 §1: the basin silts its whole coast except one rock headland. The sea lies WEST of this line; the line runs north to south and then turns east along the Saltmire's seaward bar.

river.name: the Meltwash
river.note: A1 §3.1, four reaches. Rises under the icefield's south lip, runs south down the right-of-centre, then turns west at Rooktide and dies in the Saltmire.

reaches.label: the heads
reaches.character: meltwater braids over gravel, milk-grey with rock flour

reaches.label: the upper Meltwash
reaches.character: gravel-bedded; fordable by cart in exactly one place

reaches.label: the tidal reach
reaches.character: slows, widens, silts; the sea pushes up as far as Rooktide

reaches.label: into the Saltmire
reaches.character: the river stops being a river

tidalLimit.label: head of tide
tidalLimit.note: A1 §3.1 / §4.2 zone 3: the sea reaches Rooktide's landing and no further.

ford.label: the ford
ford.note: A1 §7.1: the crossing is drawn as a ROAD symbol, not a town symbol — on a relay map it is infrastructure.

saltmire.name: the Saltmire
saltmire.note: A1 §3.1: a tidal basin of channels, mud, salt scrub and moving sandbars. No road crosses it and no keel drafts it. A1 §7.1: the channels are deliberately NOT drawn — they move.

iceEdge.note: A1 §7.2 / A1-ART-01: the parchment ends at a hard edge along the top. The map does not pretend to know what lies past the ice; this is a sheet boundary, not a coastline.

terrainPatches.label: the eastern hills
terrainPatches.note: A1 §3.2: the east rim's old timber runs up to ore heads in the eastern hills, and Thornveil is the interfluve between the Meltwash and them. Terrain only — no settlement is named here anywhere in the corpus.

zones.name: Ashvale Front
zones.note: A1 §4.3: not a band but a gradient, deepening north. Only region in the bestiary with species in all eight level bands.

gradientSegments.label: the southern lip
gradientSegments.note: old burials, settled, marked, grassed over

gradientSegments.label: the northern deep
gradientSegments.note: A1 §7.2: drawn as BARE hatch with no rows — the Bell School does not publish an inventory of its own unfinished work

towns.name: Millcross
towns.emblem: crossed roads over an empty bowl
towns.reason: The only cart-crossing of the river that splits the land, and the fork of the north road

towns.name: Gildmark
towns.emblem: a harbour scale with one pan lower
towns.reason: The only rock on a silted coast, next to the only water deep enough for a sea keel

towns.name: Embervale
towns.emblem: a caravan wheel wreathed in ember-red
towns.reason: Hill loam over a burning-stone seam, at the junction of the trade road and the coast spur

towns.name: Norhollow
towns.emblem: a hollow bell over crossed stakes
towns.reason: Where the timber line and the ore heads both begin, at the flat's eastern edge

towns.name: Rooktide
towns.emblem: a rook in flight over a rising tideline
towns.reason: The head of tide — sea barges stop, river barges start, and cargo has to change hulls

towns.name: Cindervast
towns.reason: The upland shoulder: the land's other defensible rock, guarding the only pass north

wallsOnly.note: A1 §7.2: the walls and the gate; NOTHING inside. No street grid, no squares, no statues — the Bellfaith has no tower there and will not draw a city it does not ring.

camps.name: the expedition camp
camps.note: canon.md §4: the Northern Icefield lies further north past Millcross's expedition camp.

roads.name: the trade road
roads.note: A1 §5.1: north-west off the ford, around the mire's head. canon.md §4 does not state this leg; A1 derives 2 days.

roads.name: the coastal spur
roads.note: canon.md §4: Gildmark is about 3 days from both war towns by a coastal spur. Already past the mire when it starts.

roads.name: the east-rim track
roads.note: A1 §5.1: the east-rim track joins the spur near Emberdown; the 3-day count is for the whole Norhollow → Gildmark run (~95 km), of which this leg is the eastern ~43 km.

roads.name: the crossing of the flat
roads.note: canon.md §4: sister towns roughly a day's ride apart; wartime crossing is under a day, which is exactly why the front is so lethal.

roads.name: the river road
roads.note: canon.md §4: Rooktide sits inland, south of Millcross, about 2 days. Follows the river's south bank.

roads.name: the terrace track
roads.note: A1 §5.3 quotes atlas-frontier's own placement — north-east of the ford, one morning's walk.

roads.name: up the terrace
roads.note: A1 §2: the north-east fork runs up the river terrace to the camp, Thornveil's edge and the ice. No day-count is stated anywhere in the corpus, so none is lettered.

roads.name: the Cindervast approach
roads.note: A1 §7.1: drawn as a dashed line because it is not maintained. A1 §2: the only pass north runs behind Cindervast's shoulder. No leg day-count is stated; the walking table carries the end-to-end figure instead.

relay.note: A1 §5.2: ~190 km of ridge-line and road, towers sited for line of sight at 8–10 km spacing → 21–24 relay towers, plus one tower in each of the six towns. A1 §7.1 calls the tower chain the map's actual subject, so it carries the sheet's single accent colour (bell-bronze).
relay.derivation: Towers were sampled at even intervals along the spine (Gildmark → Embervale → Millcross → Rooktide, 182 km — A1's '~190 km of ridge-line and road') and along the flat crossing, then frozen here as explicit coordinates. Sight-line spans are 7.8–8.4 km, inside A1 §5.2's 8–10 km line-of-sight budget. 27 towers are drawn: 22 on the ridgelines and roads (A1 says 21–24) plus 5 town towers. Cindervast has none — A1 §7.2: the Bellfaith will not draw a city it does not ring.
relay.withheld: A1 §7.2: the far-mirror stations sit on these same ridgelines and are deliberately NOT drawn — a Bellfaith map will not publish a Gildmark monopoly it cannot regulate.

chains.note: Gildmark → Embervale → Millcross → Rooktide, the length of the coastal spur, the trade road and the river road
Embervale → Norhollow across the Ashvale flat; branches off the trunk chain at Embervale's own tower

detachedTowers.note: A1 §7.2: the Bellfaith has no tower at Cindervast and will not draw a city it does not ring — the six-town count is towns, not standing towers. Drawn hollow, unjoined.

distances.drawnRoadsAreCentrelines: roads[].points is a simplified centre-line, so its measured length runs 0–15% short of roads[].roadKm (A1 §5.1's surveyed figure). The day-counts lettered on the sheet come from roadKm/days, never from the drawn length.
distances.note: A1 §5.1. `straightKm` is the Cartographer's figure; `computedKm` is what this file's own coordinates give, and `deltaPct` is the residual. A1 §5.3: the world preserves topology, not metric distance.

seaLane.note: A1 §7.2 / A1-ART-01: one arrow off the west edge with the trade wind's season written on it, and nothing else. canon.md §4 / V8: once a year merchantmen arrive on the trade wind.
seaLane.label: the trade wind · once a year

sheet.title: CLUSTER 1 · THE MELTWASH BASIN
sheet.subtitle: a Bellfaith relay map
sheet.hand: A1 §7: a world map is an artifact made by someone, for a purpose. This one is drawn by the institution that owns the towers, maintained because the towers must be maintained, and copied for anyone who asks.
sheet.scaleBarNote: A1 §7.1: the map has no scale bar; it has a walking table.
